questions.question: Master moved because PR #1147 was merged at 10:43 as squash 0ec727efe. That is the same tree as c3c079765, and CI was green on all checks. The round-4 panel is still reviewing exactly that tree, so its findings stay valid. Step 5 never ran, so master has no review block in the trace and no subject-list close. How should I continue?

options.label: Finish round 4, then follow-up PR (Recommended)
options.description: Let the round-4 panel finish. Whatever it finds goes into one follow-up branch off master, along with the Step 5 close: the trace review block and the ripple-check audit. That follow-up gets its own short review. Cost: one more PR. Defects the panel finds are fixed rather than left on master.

options.label: Stop the panel, close only
options.description: Stop the three round-4 reviewers now. Open a small follow-up PR off master that only adds the trace's review block (3 rounds, 17 findings) and records that no exit gate ran on the merged state. Cheapest option. Master keeps whatever round 4 would have found.

options.label: Finish round 4, file findings
options.description: Let the panel finish, but don't fix anything now. File each finding as a backlog item for later, and commit the trace review block in a docs-only follow-up. Nothing on master changes behaviour today.

options.label: Stop everything
options.description: Stop the panel and do nothing more for this delivery. The trace on master stays without its review block, which the trace-authoring rule requires, and the 3 rounds of findings stay recorded only in the PR.

questions.question: PR #1147 was merged by mistake while round 4 was still running. Master now holds the tree from c3c079765. Three rounds fixed 17 findings, and CI is green on every check. The exit gates (unprimed, whole-file, measuring on the final state) are still pending, so the loop has not converged. How should I handle it?

options.label: Keep it, converge in follow-up (Recommended)
options.description: Leave #1147 on master. Round 4 finishes against the same tree, and its fixes plus the Step 5 close go into one follow-up PR, which gets its own review until it converges. That reaches the same end state with no churn on master. Master carries any defects round 4 finds until the follow-up merges.

options.label: Revert, reopen as a new PR
options.description: I open a revert PR for 0ec727efe, which you merge. Then I push the work again as a new PR from a branch based on the reverted master, and continue the loop there with round 4's findings. Master never holds an unconverged change, at the cost of two extra commits on master and a new PR number.

options.label: Pause, I will decide
options.description: I let round 4 finish and report its findings, but change nothing and open no PR until you say which way to go.

questions.question: Sync content stream whose read() answers None (a non-blocking raw stream with no data ready): today Memory treats it as end of file and silently stores a truncated file, while async already refuses None with a marked TypeError. What should the follow-up do?

options.label: Refuse None as TypeError (Recommended)
options.description: _binary raises the caller-marked TypeError for None, the same as async. The two runtimes agree, silent truncation becomes a loud error, and spec 003 § Content stays true as written. Risk: a caller who passes a non-blocking raw stream today gets a truncated file without noticing, and will get an error instead. That stream never worked.

options.label: Document None as end of content
options.description: Keep the behaviour, and narrow § Content, MEM-020 and the PR record to say a sync read answering None ends the content. The silent truncation stays, and sync and async keep disagreeing.

questions.question: metadata passed directly to MemoryBackend.write that is truthy but not a mapping (for example metadata=5) reaches classify from inside put, and an existing target answers AlreadyExists. Store already validates metadata first, so only direct backend calls hit this. What should the follow-up do?

options.label: Narrow the claim to content (Recommended)
options.description: MEM-020, its overview row and both classify comments say nothing the caller's content raises reaches classify. No behaviour change. Metadata validation stays Store's job, and a kernel-level metadata check gets filed as a backlog item to decide separately, since it would change every kernel driver.

options.label: Refuse non-mapping metadata in the kernel
options.description: The kernel's _require_metadata raises TypeError for metadata that is not a Mapping, at the WR-010 gate's rank and before any I/O, on every driver. The claim stays true as written. This widens the follow-up to a kernel behaviour change that touches every driver, with new tests and spec text in WR-010 and BE-030.
